newsitem.title: USA: Brent crude dips in brisk late U.S. trade.
newsitem.headline: Brent crude dips in brisk late U.S. trade.

text.p: North Sea Brent crude oil dipped in brisk late U.S. dealings on Monday, traders said.
Five October exchange-for-physicals (EFP's) were transacted, four at $18.85 and one at $18.82 for a total of 550 lots.
Cash was fetching a four-cent premium to paper, putting the October cash value at $18.89-90 a barrel, down from the IPE close of $18.92.
Five November EFP's also traded, one each at $18.92 and $18.93 and three at $18.95 for a total of 900 lots.
November cash was garnering three cents over paper, putting the November value around $18.97-98, just shy of the IPE close of $19.00.
September/October Brent changed hands at minus 12 cents, while October/November moved twice at minus 14 cents.
